chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Al-Hajjal, from one of his companions, from Abu Hamza Al-Thumali, from Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, appointed an Angel over the price (of goods), managing it by His Command.
ai.seo_question: Who manages the prices of goods according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Ali ibn Al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) in al-Kafi underscores the metaphysical dimension of market dynamics, asserting that price fluctuations are not merely random but divinely orchestrated by a specific Angel. In Shia scholarly tradition, this highlights the concept of *tasarruf* (divine administration) over worldly affairs, linking economic stability to spiritual and cosmic order. It serves as a theological basis for understanding inflation and deflation as signs of divine will rather than solely human economic forces.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Al Abbas Bin marouf, from Al Hajjal, from one of his companions, from Abu Hamza Al Sumaly, 
(It has been narrated) from Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic has Allocated an Angel with the prices, managing these by His<sup>azwj</sup> Command’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn al-‘Abbas ibn Ma’ruf from al-Hajjal from certain persons of his people from abu Hamzah al-Thumaliy who has said the following: “Ali ibn Al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has assigned an angel who regulates prices by His command.’”
